title: Overdub Score - RPG Maker MZ Default Music Replacement - 75 JRPG Tracks, Same File Names
tagline: Every default BGM and ME of a new RPG Maker MZ project, re-scored in one JRPG voice under MZ's own file names.
description:
Overdub Score replaces every piece of music a new RPG Maker MZ project plays: all 48 default BGM and all 27 default ME, newly composed in one JRPG voice and filed under MZ's own file names (Theme4, Battle1, Town3, Victory1, Inn1 and the rest). Copy the pack's audio/bgm and audio/me folders over your project's, and every map, event, troop and System setting that already names a default plays this score. Nothing needs rewiring.

Tested in the engine. A blank MZ project with the two folders copied over was booted headless and asked what its own audio code loaded. At the title screen MZ decoded our Theme4 (79.09 s) where the default ran 88.00 s, and the same held for the battle, victory, defeat, game over, boat, ship and airship slots in System.json and for all 75 names played through AudioManager: 75 of 75 decoded as this pack's file, none as the default, and all 48 BGM loop points MZ parsed match the tags in the shipped files. A control run on the untouched project reads all 75 defaults, so the check can tell the two apart.

Every slot written for its job. Theme1 to Theme6 are the hero's theme, the prologue, a sorrowful theme, the title, the villain's theme and the ending. Town1 to Town8, Field1 to Field4, Ship1 to Ship3 (the boat, the ship and the airship), Dungeon1 to Dungeon7, Castle1 to Castle3, Battle1 to Battle8 (from the normal battle to the final boss) and Scene1 to Scene9 (tension, grief, comedy, mystery, rest, a chase, the villain's entrance, a farewell, daybreak). The Readme carries the full table: every file name, its title and what it was written for.

Jingles that let the music come back. MZ pauses the BGM while an ME plays and resumes it when the ME file ends, so every one of the 27 ME was cut to between 0.5 and 1.5 times the length of the default it replaces (measured on the shipped files: 1.15 to 1.40 times). No ME carries a loop tag. Every BGM carries LOOPSTART and LOOPLENGTH, which MZ reads with no plugin.

One theme in all 75 files. The score's theme, The Vow, is stated in its own shape in every file, counted by the harness in the finished MIDI. Every BGM opens on it broad, every note exactly twice its written length, before the loop point, and every loop closes on it at its own speed; every ME opens on it. Six more themes grow from it: Hearth for the towns, Horizon for the open world and its vehicles, Shadow (the theme turned upside down) for the dungeons, Steel for the battles, Crown for the castles, the villain and the great bosses, and Lament for grief and parting. 2863 statements and fragments of those themes across the pack.

What you get. 48 BGM in audio/bgm and 27 ME in audio/me (OGG Vorbis, 44.1 kHz stereo), 71:15 of music, 75 editable .mid sources under the same names, a Readme with the slot table, install steps and per engine notes, the proof reports, and a royalty free commercial licence. Back up your project's audio folders first: copying the pack over replaces the defaults under the same names, project wide.

Only the names are shared. Every note here is new and original; nothing was transcribed, arranged or derived from the default tracks. Checked: no shipped file is byte identical to any of the engine's 449 audio files, and MZ decodes every one of ours at a different length from the default it replaces. Sold for RPG Maker MZ; whether RPG Maker MV's default file names match MZ's was not measured.

Gate results. 1304 theory checks and 819 audio checks, 0 failed, and the reports ship inside the download. They say the music is correctly written, rendered and tagged. They are not a claim about taste, which is what the free files are for.

Five files are free on this page, with their MIDI: Theme4 (Overture, the title), Battle1 (Steel Drawn, every battle), Victory1 (Victory, every win), Town1 (Hearthmere, the home town) and Battle5 (The Guardian Wakes, a boss). Drop them into a test project's audio/bgm and audio/me to hear them where they will play.

The same idea for sound effects. Overdub, from the same studio, replaces the default sound effect files of an RPG Maker MZ project under their own names.

An honest note. The renders are a General MIDI reference render through a conventional soundfont, so the strings, brass, choirs and bells are the General MIDI sounds of those names; load the MIDI into your own instruments to replace them. The composition system is AI written code and no generative audio model is used anywhere.

devlog.title: Overdub Score is out: every default MZ music file, re-scored under its own name
devlog.body:
Overdub Score replaces all 75 music files a new RPG Maker MZ project plays, 48 BGM and 27 ME, with new music in one JRPG voice filed under MZ's own names. Copy two folders over your project's and every reference to a default plays this score. It is live now, with five files free to download from the page.

How it was checked. A blank MZ project with the folders copied over was booted headless and asked what it loaded: 75 of 75 default names decoded as this pack's file, none as the default, including the title (Theme4), every battle (Battle1), victory, defeat, game over and the three vehicles. Every ME lasts 1.15 to 1.40 times the default it replaces, so MZ hands the music back on time. 1304 theory checks and 819 audio checks, 0 failed, with the reports inside the download. Those numbers say the music is correctly written, rendered and tagged; they are not a claim about taste, which is what the free files (Theme4, Town1, Battle1, Battle5 and Victory1) are for.

Only the file names are shared with MZ's defaults; every note is new. The renders are a General MIDI reference render; load the MIDI into your own instruments to replace the sounds. The composition system is AI written code and no generative audio model is used.
